reading_note: The teaching unfolds the structure of life and death as two opposing organic wholes. The "beautiful tree" is the Lord's love-and-wisdom planted in the human, articulated through five discrete degrees of reception (mind → thought → reflection → counsel → teaching), each corresponding to a divine inflowing — the celestial Mind of truth, the Ambassador-thought, the living-fire reflection, the First Man's counsel, and the doctrinal teaching that bears fruit as good works. The "bitter tree" is the love of self-and-the-world, structured by the same five degrees inverted: reflection becomes the law of death, counsel becomes commerce/exchange, teaching becomes furnaces of fire, thought a stronghold of falsity, mind the bōlos of final dispersion. The arc closes with the doctrine that good and evil are NOT two branches of one root: they do not originate from one another nor from one man, but ascend to two distinct aeons. Souls that ascend pass through the five faculties of the beautiful tree to the Mind of truth; those who refuse fall to the clod and the darkness without repentance. The single arc: the structure of regeneration vs. damnation as two complete, non-derivative organic forms.
